tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-06 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Neutral. Component 1 regime (rates-led late cycle: Richard's view 16-Sep-26, rates and yields rising, inflation high, consumer confidence low, downside skew; sources absent): regulated, leveraged, long-duration assets are hit by his discount-rate line, offset by defensive demand; Ports lead at A but that is leadership only. Relative strength C now, C prior. No tilt.

sector.why: Underweight, carried; the special topic 'The Sector Memo on telecoms relative strength: pullback or structurally impaired?' ties this row to the same yield leg as the telecoms rows (the US ten-year under 4.5% would favour both), and nothing read this week moves the ten-year from the 5% last read. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: D now, F prior. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). One live holding, Helios Towers, now 7.21% and the largest position (from 5.17%), Thematic Fit/Momentum D through this row and Bottom-up B on its own case; the row is a blunt instrument on it and component 5 says so. Counter-case: contracted, inflation-linked revenue is the visible cash the regime pays for, and towers rally hardest when rates peak. Back to C on the ten-year under 4.5% or the Fed path marked down.

geography.why: Underweight, carried unchanged with the reason strengthened. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the spillover from France to Italy is the new fact this week (Goldman, 16 Oct, 'tentative spillover to Italy'), and the Italian listings in the Pool are bank-heavy (Monte dei Paschi, Credito Emiliano, Mediobanca) beside global businesses (Eni, Saipem, Tenaris, STMicroelectronics, Technoprobe, Reply). Not Double Underweight because Goldman also says contagion risk is lower than in 2011-15, its fragmentation index shows risk 'remains limited', and Southern European banks are healthier; relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to F if the fragmentation index rises or the Italian premium is read above 150 basis points; back to C under 100.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
